cipher.name: VowelRotatorAndConsonantAtbash
cipher.idea: To maximize the model's reasoning capability while maintaining a strong obfuscation layer, this cipher uses two simple, highly deterministic rules: vowels are rotated forward by 1 position in the vowel sequence, and consonants are mirrored using a standard Atbash-style mapping within the consonant set. Case is preserved. Digits, spaces, and punctuation remain completely unchanged.
cipher.encrypt_rules:
1. Identify if a character is a letter. If not, leave it unchanged.
2. If it is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive), shift it forward to the next vowel in the sequence: a -> e, e -> i, i -> o, o -> u, u -> a. Preserve the original case.
3. If it is a consonant, mirror it within the consonant-only alphabet (b, c, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, q, r, s, t, v, w, x, y, z). The mapping is: b<->z, c<->y, d<->x, f<->w, g<->v, h<->t, j<->s, k<->r, l<->q, m<->p, n<->n. Preserve the original case.
cipher.decrypt_rules:
1. Identify if a character is a letter. If not, leave it unchanged.
2. If it is a vowel, shift it backward to the previous vowel in the sequence: a -> u, e -> a, i -> e, o -> i, u -> o. Preserve the original case.
3. If it is a consonant, apply the same mirror mapping: b<->z, c<->y, d<->x, f<->w, g<->v, h<->t, j<->s, k<->r, l<->q, m<->p, n<->n. Preserve the original case.
